title: Circuit schema v0.4
description: A circuit says what is connected (nets), what is placed where (elements, ports) and how it is drawn (wires, junctions). Coordinates are integer grid steps (1 step = 0.25 cm); x points right and y points UP. Structure only: semantic checks (pins exist, drawing realises the nets, one driver per net) are a separate lint.

schema.description: Format and version. Readers reject an unknown major version.

grid_cm.description: Grid step the coordinates assume, so a reader can detect a mismatch.

ports.description: The circuit's own inputs and outputs.

nets.description: Connectivity: net id to the endpoints it joins. The truth for simulation.

wires.description: Drawn connections. Routing is specified (intent), not stored (corners).

groups.description: Buses for display: name to port ids, most significant bit first.

labels.description: Free text such as titles and notes.

weight.description: Line weight the figure is drawn with. Default regular.

theme.description: Theme the figure is drawn with. Default default. Private themes are never named in a saved figure.

levels.description: Optional: the colour the user chose for each logic level (0, 1, X unknown, Z floating). An absent key, or an absent light or dark colour, means the theme's default. A drawing annotation only: it never changes the nets or the simulation.

style.description: Optional, figure-level: how the figure is drawn. It never changes the nets or the simulation, and a simulator may ignore it. Absent means regular weight and the default theme.

annotations.description: circuit/0.3 only. Optional editor data that is not circuit structure (frames, net labels, slide, tool settings): one key per tool in lowercase kebab-case, e.g. annotations["schematic-editor"], each an object that tool owns. The simulator and validators check nothing inside it. `groups` stays reserved for buses.

modules.description: circuit/0.4 only. Hierarchy: module name to a sub-circuit drawn and connected like the top level. A `block` element with params.module is one instance of it; its pins are the module's port ids. Modules may contain instances of other modules but never, directly or through others, of themselves. The simulator and the analysis flatten instances before they run (an instance's elements and nets become <instance>_<id>). Checked by validate/ (both languages).

module.description: A sub-circuit (circuit/0.4): the same fields as the top level, without the figure-level ones.

id.description: One namespace for elements, ports, junctions and wires. Never contains a dot, so "fa0.Cout" is always a pin and a bare id is a port or junction.

ref.description: An endpoint: "element.pin", or a bare port or junction id. The pin part allows + and - (voltage source).

light.description: Colour on the light theme, as #RRGGBB.

dark.description: Colour on the dark theme, as #RRGGBB.

tex.description: TeX maths such as "$A_0$", limited to what MathJax 4 also renders.

type.description: Element name in the symbol pack, e.g. and_gate.

rotation.description: Degrees counter-clockwise about the element origin. Default 0.

mirror.description: Added in v0.2. If true, the element is flipped left-to-right (x negated in the element's own frame) before rotation is applied. Default false.

level.description: Optional drawing annotation: the element's body is drawn in this logic level's colour (0, 1, X unknown, Z floating), as strings. Its leads keep the colour of the wire they connect to. Not a simulation result; never changes the nets; a simulator may ignore it.

params.description: Per-instance parameters, e.g. {"delay": {"Cout": 3}}. For type "block" see $defs/block_params.

pin_name.description: The pin part of a ref, so "blockid.name" works in nets and wires.

label.description: Optional display label drawn inside the block next to the pin.

block_pin.description: A block pin: its name, or an object with the name and an optional display label.

block_params.description: Parameters of the built-in element type "block", a configurable labelled box that is not in the symbol pack. Pin rule: pins on a side are one module apart and centred on that side; each side is at least (pins + 1) modules long, so w and h are raised to that minimum by the renderer. Because w and h are whole modules, every pin lands on a whole grid step. One module is 2 grid steps. Pins are listed in drawing order: left and right top to bottom, top and bottom left to right.

label.description: A LaTeX string drawn in the block. May be empty.

module.description: circuit/0.4 only. The block is an instance of this entry in `modules`; its pins must be exactly that module's port ids.

id.description: Also the default net name it joins.

dir.description: Inputs are driven by the scenario.

side.description: Which side of `at` the label sits.

route.description: circuit/0.3 only. Optional routing mode for each leg, from the start through every waypoint to the end. `straight` joins the stops directly; `auto` uses the orthogonal router. If absent, every leg is auto-routed.

first.description: Direction of the first auto-routed leg.

arrow.description: Optional drawing annotation: arrowheads at the wire's start (from), end (to) or both. Default none. Never changes the nets.

bus.description: Optional drawing annotation: a label such as "N" or "4", drawn as a slash across the wire with that label. Never changes the nets.

level.description: Optional drawing annotation: the logic level this wire is drawn to show (0, 1, X unknown, Z floating), as strings. It only says how the wire is drawn in this figure. It is not a simulation result, never changes the nets, and a simulator may ignore it. With no level the wire is drawn in the default colour.

on.description: Id of the wire it taps.
